song.title: Lil Baby, Gunna - Drip Too Hard [Dance]

sections.rationale: Bars 1-3 are effectively silent (combined_intensity 0.078, 0.033, 0.052) and bar 4 is flagged is_build as the mix lifts to 0.22 before the bass and kick arrive at bar 5. The player is cold and the mechanic is new, so the first pattern is the smallest thing the language can say -- two arrows, one per strong beat, three misses forgiven, which at two inputs means the encounter cannot be failed at all. The second pattern doubles the load onto the build, so the first time the player is asked for four inputs is the first time there is a drop to ask over. Both patterns lock movement (movementScale 0): the seal travels with the body, so there is nowhere to walk to and letting the player drift would only add noise to the reading.

Bars 7-12 are the first sustained loud passage (combined_intensity 0.574, 0.610, 0.649, 0.692, 0.666, 0.684) with energy_peak anchors at bars 7, 9 and 11, and bar 13 is the energy_drop that ends it. This is where the song's own subdivision is introduced: AP52 is a triplet walk, five steps at two-thirds of a beat each, which is the swung figure the vocal is using over the half-time grid. AP53 answers it with a long call and a short reply so the player learns that phrase length is information rather than a fixed count. Both resolve on real downbeats -- the analysis put this track's bar phase two beats into the grid bar, so a phrase at bar N beat 3 is the downbeat and an accent four grid beats later is the next one.

Bar 14 is a release into the first real valley of the record: bars 15-18 fall to 0.571, 0.413, 0.190, 0.247 with vocal_exit and vocal_entry back to back at bar 17, and the rebuild starts at bar 19. Both patterns here are slow sways -- four arrows inside a beat and a half, two misses forgiven -- so the hands keep moving while the mix is away. The recovery is placed on the music's own rest rather than on a difficulty budget: the section after it opens at 0.70 intensity, and a player who spent the valley reading gently is ready for it.

Bars 19-24 rebuild through is_build flags to energy_peaks at bars 20, 22 and 24, then bar 25 releases. AP54 is the half-time pattern: a doubled cell, a beat and a half of authored silence, then a second doubled cell into the accent. The hole is the teaching point -- the player has to hold position through the gap instead of filling it -- and it is placed here because this is the first place in the song with enough space around the phrase to hear what is missing. AP39 drops back to four arrows and lets the section land softly before the climb.

Bars 27-31 build to energy_peaks at 28 and 30, bar 32 releases to 0.352 and bars 33-35 start the longest climb in the song. AP55 is the syncopation pattern -- six arrows in three beats with the second one missing -- and the skip is what makes it read as syncopation rather than as a run, because the hand wants to press on the beat that is not there. AP41 follows with a six-arrow circuit at the same density so the section ends on continuous input rather than on a hole, which is the shape the climb into bar 36 actually has.

Bars 33-40 are the loudest consecutive run in the track (0.580, 0.585, 0.603, 0.629, 0.677, 0.702, 0.666, 0.697) with peaks at 34, 36, 38 and 40, and phrase_007 (bars 37-44) carries the highest relative_intensity in the song at 0.938. AP56 is seven arrows, one per half-beat, straight into the accent: after the swing and the syncopation, the loudest bars ask for an even stream a player can lock onto, and the pressure is the tempo rather than the shape. AP28 then answers on the backbeat, so the two rounds of the peak do not resolve in the same place.

Bar 44 is a release and bars 45-46 are a valley (0.211, 0.266) before the rebuild at 47. This is the second and last true rest in the record, so it gets the two gentlest patterns in the language: a pendulum and a short echo, both under five arrows, both two-miss forgiving. Everything after this point is loud to the end, which is why the recovery is spent here rather than later.

Bars 47-52 rebuild to energy_peaks at 48, 50 and 52, then 53-54 release before the final lift. AP57 is the swung walk from the first drop, but where it used to end it now doubles -- four triplet steps then three in the last beat -- so the player recognises the opening and then has to accelerate inside a subdivision they thought they knew. AP44 closes the section with a doubled-cell machine at sixteenth spacing, the densest thing in the level before the boss.

Bars 55-58 are the last build (peaks at 56 and 58) and bars 59-60 are the release that ends the record; bar 61 is a vocal_exit and bars 61-68 sit at combined_intensity 0.03-0.09, which is why the level stops at 60 rather than charting the eight near-silent bars the director's own generated level covers. AP58 is the only dance pattern in the library with three rounds -- an even six, a swung six, and a short three that resolves on the last beat of the pattern -- so the finale cannot be memorised as a list, only read. It is the last thing the song asks for and it lands on the last musical bar.
